I ported the calculator to Kotlin and `node check.mjs` passes all 6 example cases. I also ran the original JS and the Kotlin port on three random inputs of 200,000 lines each, using the checker's own generator. I added very deep nesting (100,000 levels of parentheses and 100,000 unary minuses) and some overflow edge cases. The output was byte-for-byte identical, and each run took about 0.14s.

- **`src/calc/Calc.kt`**: the evaluator. Like the original, it parses without recursion, so very deep n
